reviews.review:
One nice feature of the co-op game is if you have no one to join your group then you can play with bots.
Did not realize that the first mission is nearly impossible to finish. After several attempts finally go it done.
Next mission I guess the Devs though it would be challenging if you could not get more ammo.  Maybe its a bug. After I played trough each mission I thought the next one would be different. Sadly they are almost the same. The game gets repetitive and boring fast.
The game mechanics was taken from Remnant from the Ashes which is a much better game.

The base game was decent, but only if you're an Aliens franchise fan. It quickly becomes repetitive: drop into a map, follow the objective prompts, and along the way plow through mobs of xenomorphs. The sound and art design are superb; I felt like I was in the movie at times. However, I'm not as big a fan of the "mutated" bugs; that felt like nothing more than an effort to add interest to a repetitive game model. I also disliked the planetside missions; they just didn't feel like Aliens. I prefer cramped, humid, slimed-up corridors.

The DLC was an extraordinary waste of money. They only provide a bunch of irrelevant cosmetic items and a VERY short, three-mission campaign that I burned through in two brief sessions.

Regarding the teams, the public squad matchmaking is spotty. As with all such conventions, you'll get paired with good teammates sometimes, and horrible teammates at other times. Some people play the objectives; some don't. I do appreciate the option to team up with bots, but they're not nearly as smart about reviving as human opponents (they'll try to revive you in a room filled with enemies, and often die themselves in so doing). 

I also dislike the pattern they used for hidden items. The missions are not constructed to allow time for exploration, especially when you're playing with other impatient humans who may not know why you're digressing from the objectives. Also, these hidden items can be very difficult to find, especially when you're being mobbed. It's a good idea, just not very well executed.

All in all, if you're a fan of Aliens, you'll get enough fun out of this game to justify purchasing the base game. But I suggest you skip the much-lower-value DLCs.
